mikhail_tal.name: Mikhail Tal
mikhail_tal.title: GM
mikhail_tal.description: The Magician from Riga. You play for dynamic attacking chances, avoid piece trades, and keep queens on to create threats. Your games are chaotic and exciting.
mikhail_tal.study_tip: Study Tal's games from the 1959 Candidates Tournament and his matches against Botvinnik. Focus on the psychology of pressure over pure calculation.

anatoly_karpov.name: Anatoly Karpov
anatoly_karpov.title: GM
anatoly_karpov.description: The Boa Constrictor. You accumulate small advantages, trade into favorable endgames, and squeeze opponents without ever giving them counterplay.
anatoly_karpov.study_tip: Study Karpov vs Kasparov 1984-1985 World Championship. Read 'Karpov's Strategic Wins' by Tibor Karolyi.

garry_kasparov.name: Garry Kasparov
garry_kasparov.title: GM
garry_kasparov.description: The Greatest of All Time. You combine deep preparation, dynamic pawn structures, and ferocious attacking play. You seek the initiative at every opportunity.
garry_kasparov.study_tip: Work through 'My Great Predecessors' by Kasparov. Study his Sicilian Najdorf games for attacking templates.

tigran_petrosian.name: Tigran Petrosian
tigran_petrosian.title: GM
tigran_petrosian.description: Iron Tigran. You excel at prophylaxis — preventing opponent plans before they start. You trade pieces to neutralise attacks and grind in quiet positions.
tigran_petrosian.study_tip: Study Petrosian's 1963 World Championship match vs Botvinnik. Focus on his exchange sacrifices for long-term positional compensation.

magnus_carlsen.name: Magnus Carlsen
magnus_carlsen.title: GM
magnus_carlsen.description: The World Champion. You play universally well across all phases, preferring to outplay opponents in long technical endgames. Patience and precision define your style.
magnus_carlsen.study_tip: Study Carlsen's endgame technique in his World Championship defences. 'Magnus Carlsen: Move by Move' by Cyrus Lakdawala is excellent.

bobby_fischer.name: Bobby Fischer
bobby_fischer.title: GM
bobby_fischer.description: The American Legend. You seek perfect, logical chess — optimal piece placement, concrete calculation, and converting advantages with clinical precision.
bobby_fischer.study_tip: Study 'My 60 Memorable Games' by Fischer. Pay special attention to his bishop vs knight endgame technique.

viswanathan_anand.name: Viswanathan Anand
viswanathan_anand.title: GM
viswanathan_anand.description: The Tiger of Madras. You play fast and tactically sharp, relying on opening preparation and rapid calculation to outmanoeuvre opponents before they settle.
viswanathan_anand.study_tip: Study Anand's rapid chess games and his Sicilian Najdorf preparation. His 2007-2010 World Championship performances are instructive.

ding_liren.name: Ding Liren
ding_liren.title: GM
ding_liren.description: The World Champion from China. You play solidly and precisely, converting technical advantages with excellent endgame technique and avoiding unnecessary risks.
ding_liren.study_tip: Study Ding's tournament wins, especially his 2023 Candidates performance. Focus on his rook endgame conversions.

hikaru_nakamura.name: Hikaru Nakamura
hikaru_nakamura.title: GM
hikaru_nakamura.description: The American Speedster. You attack relentlessly, keep maximum pieces on the board, and play for complications where your superior tactical vision shines.
hikaru_nakamura.study_tip: Study Nakamura's speed chess games and his offbeat opening choices. His attacking games in the King's Indian are excellent attacking templates.

fabiano_caruana.name: Fabiano Caruana
fabiano_caruana.title: GM
fabiano_caruana.description: The American Challenger. You rely on deep opening preparation and sharp theoretical lines. Your games combine concrete calculation with strategic understanding.
fabiano_caruana.study_tip: Study Caruana's 2018 World Championship match preparation. His Petroff Defence and Sicilian Najdorf play are deeply instructive.

paul_morphy.name: Paul Morphy
paul_morphy.title: GM
paul_morphy.description: The Pride and Sorrow of Chess. You prioritise rapid development and open lines for your pieces, attacking brilliantly with fully coordinated forces.
paul_morphy.study_tip: Study Morphy's famous Opera Game and his matches against Harrwitz and Anderssen. 'The Genius of Paul Morphy' by Chris Ward is highly recommended.

jose_capablanca.name: José Capablanca
jose_capablanca.title: GM
jose_capablanca.description: The Human Chess Machine. You play with effortless clarity, trading into technically won endgames and converting advantages with perfect technique.
jose_capablanca.study_tip: Study Capablanca's 1921 World Championship match vs Lasker and his 'Chess Fundamentals' book. His rook endgame technique is the gold standard.

mikhail_botvinnik.name: Mikhail Botvinnik
mikhail_botvinnik.title: GM
mikhail_botvinnik.description: The Patriarch of Soviet Chess. You combine rigorous preparation, deep strategic planning, and concrete calculation — approaching chess scientifically.
mikhail_botvinnik.study_tip: Study Botvinnik's self-annotated games in 'One Hundred Selected Games'. His Nimzo-Indian and Queen's Gambit games are strategically rich.

vasily_smyslov.name: Vasily Smyslov
vasily_smyslov.title: GM
vasily_smyslov.description: The Endgame Artist. You seek harmony in piece placement and trade into positions where your superb endgame technique gives you a natural edge.
vasily_smyslov.study_tip: Study Smyslov's 1957 World Championship win over Botvinnik. His rook and pawn endgames are textbook examples of technique.

alexander_alekhine.name: Alexander Alekhine
alexander_alekhine.title: GM
alexander_alekhine.description: The World Champion Attacker. You create incredibly complex positions, sacrificing material freely for long-term attacking chances. Your combinations are visionary.
alexander_alekhine.study_tip: Study Alekhine's 'My Best Games of Chess 1908-1937'. His attacking games vs Nimzowitsch and Capablanca reveal extraordinary combinational depth.
